comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–27 OER, Article 13 and Annex II, confirms the exact IPS specialisation without Arabic as a 180-EC route: 120 EC required major courses (60 EC in the first year, 45 EC in the second year and 15 EC in the third), two restricted 15-EC THRW modules, and 30 EC of genuine free minor space. This reconstruction chooses the first-listed second-year Religie en Zorg module and first-listed third-year Wereldbeelden, Natuur en Klimaat module only as neutral instances of the two-module requirement. Each consists of three 5-EC courses; alternatives are permitted, including a PPS module under Article 13. The 0-EC RADAr language test is not included in the credit total. The public year-two prospectus separately lists a 15-EC free choice as well as a 15-EC module although the 45-EC required courses already leave only 15 EC in that year; the adopted OER controls the 180-EC total and permits 30 EC free minor space across later years. The optional Arabic route instead devotes 25 EC to residence in Cairo or Rabat and has only 5 EC free minor space; it is not combined with this general route. The formal OER listing and public programme overview were rechecked on 13 October 2026; the route and credit reconstruction remain current.

progressionAssessment.rationale: All 24 unique courses use an exact available cohort term and the only formal prerequisite, Law, Society & Justice for Comparative Constitutional Law, is completed three semesters earlier. PPD is in Year 1 and seven courses are level 300. Introductory philosophy, sociology, politics, archaeology and law precede the corresponding advanced interpretive, conflict, constitutional and heritage work where the timetable permits; the no-prerequisite civil-society course follows Introduction to Sociology.

alternativeSelection.assessment: One complete related-fields programme passes the evidence, coherence, course-contribution and schedule gates. It studies how myth, literature, philosophy and visual heritage address belief and religious expression, then examines rights, migration, identity, institutions and conflict through law and the social sciences. It does not claim sustained Islam, Arabic, theology, sacred-text or religious-studies training. The first additional direction—Arabic, Islamic sources and theology—is not feasible because UCR has no Arabic acquisition, Qur'anic/source-language interpretation or Islamic-theology sequence, so production stops at one. The separately evidenced religion-and-environment and religion-and-healthcare directions were also assessed: UCR can supply sustainability, ethics, psychology and public-health courses, but lacks the religion-specific framing needed for either to organise a credible 24-course programme.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both provide historical-cultural encounters with Islam in the wider Mediterranean; UCR focuses on artistic exchange with Islamic courts and does not survey Islamic history in Europe and the Middle East.
Both use philosophical analysis for questions of belief and meaning; UCR is a general Western-philosophy introduction, not philosophy of religious studies.
UCR has no sustained study of Muhammad and Islamic revelation.
UCR has no introductory course dedicated to Islam as a religious tradition.
UCR encounters religious narratives and objects but does not provide a world-religions survey.
Comparative myth and literature do not reproduce sacred-text hermeneutics.
UCR has no course in Islamic intellectual traditions.
Social inquiry does not become a course in lived Islam.
UCR has no religion-specific course on text and authority.
UCR has no sustained course in alternative spirituality or conspiracy thinking.
Media & Race supplies an identity-and-power lens but does not directly study religion, media and popular culture.
UCR has no Islamic theology course.
Both establish a framework for law, society and public questions; UCR does not provide the comparator's religion-specific introduction.
Both address migration, identity and public life; UCR studies migrant inclusion and civil society generally rather than Islam as a transnational religious space.
The UCR programme analyses identity and power through related disciplines but has no religion-specific sequence.
UCR politics, law and sociology provide contemporary frameworks, not a historical course on religion in the public domain.
UCR has academic and professional development but not a 10-EC religion-and-theology skills sequence.
UCR qualitative methodology can support empirical inquiry but does not itself study religion in the Netherlands.
UCR methods courses do not reproduce a 10-EC research project on religion and society.
The comparator's humanities-in-practice component remains visible as a distinct requirement.
The comparator requires a 10-EC independent final work in its field; UCR optional independent research is shown in parallel outside the scheduled 180 EC.

The selected restricted Religion and Care module retains its religious, textual, ritual and psychology-of-religion framing; adjacent UCR ethics, psychology and health courses were not inserted as substitutes.
The selected restricted Worldviews, Nature and Climate module retains its religious and spiritual framing; general sustainability courses were not inserted to imitate it.
The comparator's 30 EC of genuine free minor space remains visible without invented content.

notes.text: Radboud Islam, Politics and Society combines sustained study of Islamic history, sources, thought, theology and lived religion with religious-studies methods and political-social analysis. UCR can study how narratives, philosophy and visual heritage treat belief and religious expression, and it can analyse identity, migration, rights and conflict through law and the social sciences. It does not teach Arabic, Islam as a sustained disciplinary object, Islamic theology, Qur'anic source interpretation or religion-specific methods. The UCR programme is therefore a related-fields response rather than an Islam or Religious Studies curriculum.

The external no-Arabic route contains a fixed Islam and Religious Studies major, two restricted 15-EC thematic modules, 30 EC of free minor space and a 10-EC final work. UCR assembles related perspectives across individually selected courses and has no scheduled religion-specific thesis; optional independent research is shown only as the standardized comparison element.
